SharedFlowBundle.name: SF-Signature-Validator
SharedFlowBundle.Description: Single entry point for signature validation at the gateway (the API itself provides no validation method). Calling API proxies set the signature.verify.type flow variable (jwt | cavage | xmldsig) and invoke this shared flow via FlowCallout; it routes to the matching sub-step. JWT/JWS verification itself is fully native (VerifyJWS, no JS): KnownHeaders and whether the scheme is compact or detached both resolve per-proxy from the shared KVM "signature" via ref — the calling proxy only ever stages the JWS itself, never a detached flag or the response payload, both of which AM-JWT-Verify-Set-Detached-Payload stages from response.content automatically when KVM says detached — with KnownHeaders/IgnoreCriticalHeaders enforcing RFC 7515 §4.1.11's "crit" rule. The verification public key comes from one of two KVM-configured sources, exactly one per proxy (see EV-JWT-Verify-Parse-Config): a static publicKeyPem (no network call — populated out-of-band whenever the certificate is issued/rotated, since VerifyJWS's own does not resolve a dynamic ref at runtime, confirmed against a live Apigee instance, and there's no other way to reach KeyStore key material from inside a running proxy), or a jwksUri (JS-JWT-Verify-Extract-Kid reads "kid" from the JWS header; LookupCache-JWT-Verify-JWKS-Key checks a shared cache keyed on jwksUri+kid before paying for a fetch; on a miss, SC-JWT-Verify-Fetch-JWKS fetches the document, JS-JWT-Verify-Resolve-JWKS-Key matches by kid and repackages the RSA key as PEM, and PopulateCache-JWT-Verify-JWKS-Key caches it for next time) — both sources land in the same signature.verify.jwt.publicKey.pem variable VerifyJWS reads. Cavage verifies everything achievable without real RSA/ECDSA math (the signing string) natively in JS, and faults via a clearly marked NI-Cavage-Verify-Signature placeholder for the actual cryptographic check, which needs a JavaCallout — Apigee has no native policy for raw-string signature verification, and JS can't reach KeyStore key material to do that math itself. XML-DSig verification IS fully implemented: one JavaCallout (JC-XmlDsig-Verify-Signature) does canonicalization, digest, and the SignatureValue check together, using the JDK's built-in JSR 105 implementation (javax.xml.crypto.dsig — no extra library beyond the Apigee SDK). Its verification public key is PEM-in-KVM too, same pattern and reason as JWT.
